items.changed: Updated 20 Nov: Akvan weakened before landfall; more than 300,000 people evacuated.
items.title: Cyclone Akvan weakens as it nears Odisha coast; 300,000 evacuated
items.why: India's weather department (IMD) says Akvan weakened early on Friday to a cyclonic storm, with winds of 80 to 90 km/h, as it neared Gopalpur in Odisha. Landfall is expected by midday. Odisha's chief minister, Mohan Charan Majhi, says more than 300,000 people have been moved to safety.
items.matters: Extremely heavy rain is forecast in north Andhra Pradesh and south Odisha; dozens of trains have been cancelled.

items.title: Japan's core inflation rises to 2.2% in October, above central bank target
items.why: Consumer prices in Japan excluding fresh food rose 2.2% in the year to October, up from 2.1% in September but just below the 2.3% economists expected, government data showed on Friday. Headline inflation rose to 2.3% after household energy subsidies ended in September.
items.matters: Many investors expect the Bank of Japan to raise its 1.25% interest rate in December, making borrowing dearer.

items.title: Fiona, Cincinnati Zoo's famous hippo, dies after swallowing a visitor's hat
items.why: Cincinnati Zoo, in the US state of Ohio, said on Thursday that Fiona, its nine-year-old Nile hippo, had died. A knitted hat thrown by a visitor was blown into her enclosure by a ceiling fan; vets spent about 11 days trying to help her pass it.
items.matters: Born six weeks early in 2017, she became an internet sensation as people around the world followed her fight to survive.

items.title: Ben Shelton reaches ATP Finals semi-finals for the first time
items.why: American Ben Shelton beat Spain's Rafael Jodar 7-6, 7-5 in Turin, Italy, on Thursday, then went through as runner-up in his group when Alexander Zverev beat France's Arthur Fils. Shelton, 24, will face Carlos Alcaraz in the semi-finals.
items.matters: He is the youngest American to reach the last four since Andy Roddick in 2004, the ATP says.

items.title: House panel says US approved over 879,000 AI chips for China
items.why: The US House Foreign Affairs Committee released licence records on Thursday showing the Commerce Department approved more than 879,000 of 3.4 million requested Nvidia H200 and AMD chips for Chinese firms between December 2025 and May 2026. Buyers included Tencent and Alibaba.
items.matters: It is unclear how many licences led to shipments; Nvidia says it has since stopped sending H200 chips to China.

items.title: Somalia expels UAE ambassador, accusing Abu Dhabi of interference
items.why: Somalia's government gave the United Arab Emirates' ambassador 72 hours to leave on Thursday and recalled its own envoy, accusing the UAE of "blatant aggression" and of backing regional states that oppose the federal government. The UAE called the move escalatory and hostile.
items.matters: The UAE runs ports at Berbera, Bosaso and Kismayo, in regions where Somalia's federal government has little control.

items.title: Haiti police say raid killed at least 34 suspected gang members
items.why: Haiti's national police say an operation on Thursday in Martissant, a gang-held district of the capital, Port-au-Prince, killed at least 34 suspected gang members, with no officers or civilians hurt. It involved a government task force supported by a private firm founded by Erik Prince.
items.matters: The UN says more than 2,250 people were killed in security operations in Haiti in the first nine months of 2026.

items.title: Kushner says Russia 'comfortable' with NATO-style guarantees for Ukraine
items.why: US envoy Jared Kushner said during a "Coalition of the Willing" meeting of more than 25 leaders in the German capital, Berlin, on Thursday that Russia is comfortable with post-war guarantees for Ukraine based on NATO's Article 5. Russia has not commented. Trump joined by phone after meeting Putin.
items.matters: Zelensky wants Europe in US-led talks with Russia; France's Macron urged allies to "reopen the question" of Ukraine joining NATO.

items.title: Brazil recognises Indigenous land of Amazon chief Raoni
items.why: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva visited 94-year-old Kayapó leader Raoni Metuktire in Mato Grosso state on Thursday as Brazil declared the 362,000-hectare Kapôt Nhinore territory the permanent possession of the Mẽbêngôkre and Yudjá peoples. The Indigenous peoples minister says about 84% of it is forest.
items.matters: It is a step towards full legal protection; more than 200 farms overlap the land, and rural producers oppose it.

items.title: US sells first deep-sea mining leases off American Samoa despite court ruling
items.why: The US Interior Department auctioned two areas covering about 31 million acres (12.5 million hectares) of Pacific seabed off American Samoa on Thursday, for $6m in total. A federal judge ruled on Monday that a US fisheries agency broke endangered species law in approving the sale.
items.matters: Miners want nodules rich in nickel and cobalt for batteries; conservation groups say mining could harm whales, turtles and corals.

sources.name: US Bureau of Ocean Energy Management

items.title: Blackpool sack head coach hours after wishing him happy birthday
items.why: English third-tier club Blackpool wished head coach Ian Evatt a happy 45th birthday on social media at 9:08am on Thursday, then announced his departure at 4pm. The team is 20th of 24 in League One after one win in its last 10 league games.

items.title: UK tribunal rules government must confirm secret encryption order to Apple
items.why: Britain's Investigatory Powers Tribunal ruled on Thursday that the Home Office must confirm it issued Apple a secret notice seeking access to encrypted user data. It rejected the government's claim that confirming this would harm national security, calling that "fanciful".
items.matters: Apple withdrew its strongest iCloud encryption option for UK users in 2025 over the dispute; a fuller hearing is due in 2027.

items.title: Russian drone attack on Kyiv kills one and damages two embassies
items.why: Russian drones struck Ukraine's capital, Kyiv, on Thursday, killing a 26-year-old man and injuring at least four people, Ukrainian officials say. The Dutch and Austrian embassies were damaged and windows broke at St Volodymyr's Cathedral; embassy staff were unhurt.
items.matters: Russia's embassy in the Netherlands says it was "not a targeted attack".

items.title: South Africa's central bank holds interest rate at 7.25% in split vote
items.why: The South African Reserve Bank kept its main rate at 7.25% on Thursday, with four policy committee members voting to hold and three for a rise. Governor Lesetja Kganyago said inflation rose to 5.2% in October, driven mainly by fuel costs.
items.matters: Banks' prime lending rate stays at 10.75%; the governor says the bank will not hesitate to raise rates if needed.

items.title: Houthi attack damages Riyadh skyscraper as rebels push towards Aden
items.why: Saudi Arabia says a Houthi attack on Thursday damaged several floors of the Public Investment Fund tower in Riyadh, with no injuries. The Saudi-led coalition says it dealt with a missile threat and initial checks point to falling debris. Houthi forces are advancing on Aden, Yemen's government base.
items.matters: The Houthis claim cruise-missile strikes on Riyadh's airport and financial district; Saudi Arabia calls it a terrorist attack.

items.changed: Updated 20 Nov: a new draft dropped all mention of fossil fuels.
items.title: COP31 draft deal drops mention of fossil fuels on eve of deadline
items.why: A shorter draft deal published on Thursday at the UN climate summit in Antalya, Türkiye, no longer mentions fossil fuels and drops a $120bn-a-year target for adaptation finance, Reuters reports. Talks are due to end on Friday; talks leader Chris Bowen says he will consult through the night.
items.matters: Campaigners say the text goes backwards; any deal needs the agreement of nearly 200 countries, and summits often overrun.

items.title: Alibaba's AI cloud sales jump 53% but adjusted profit misses forecasts
items.why: China's Alibaba said on Thursday that revenue from its AI cloud and computing unit rose 53% to 61bn yuan (about $9.1bn) in the July–September quarter. Group revenue rose 10% to 271.5bn yuan, while sales in its China e-commerce business fell 5%.
items.matters: Adjusted earnings per share were below analysts' forecasts as Alibaba spends heavily on AI computing.

items.title: Infantino to face France's Diallo and Japan's Tashima in FIFA election
items.why: FIFA said on Thursday it has received three candidacies for its presidency: Gianni Infantino, in office since 2016, French federation head Philippe Diallo and Japan's Kohzo Tashima. Its 211 member associations vote in Rabat, Morocco, on 18 March 2027.
items.matters: It is Infantino's first contested election since 2016; an electoral committee will now check whether the candidates are eligible.

items.title: Bangladesh measles deaths pass 1,330 as outbreak continues among children
items.why: Seven more children died with measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours to Thursday morning, taking the toll since 15 March to 1,336, Bangladesh's health directorate says; 105 deaths are laboratory-confirmed. More than 253,000 suspected cases have been reported, most in Dhaka division.
items.matters: Officials say limited testing makes the true number of infections hard to know; most figures come from hospital admissions.

items.title: South Korea's top court orders retrial of ex-PM Han over martial law
items.why: South Korea's Supreme Court on Thursday overturned former prime minister Han Duck-soo's 15-year prison sentence for his role in ex-president Yoon Suk Yeol's December 2024 martial law bid, and sent the case back to the Seoul High Court. Han remains in custody.
items.matters: The court found too little evidence he meant to subvert the constitution before the decree, but upheld findings on his later actions.

items.title: Yunus's family home set on fire as Hasina's party holds Bangladesh shutdown
items.why: Police say the ancestral home of former interim leader Muhammad Yunus in Bangladesh's port city of Chittagong was set alight late on Wednesday; no one was hurt. On Thursday, Sheikh Hasina's banned Awami League held a nationwide "lockdown"; police say two ruling-party members were killed.
items.matters: Hasina, sentenced to death in absentia, says she will return from India in December; the government refused her a passport.

items.title: Kenya's world marathon champion Peres Jepchirchir banned for three years for doping
items.why: The Athletics Integrity Unit said on Thursday it had banned Peres Jepchirchir, the reigning world and former Olympic champion, after she admitted using the blood booster EPO. The ban runs from 20 October; she loses her Sydney Marathon title from August.
items.matters: Her ban was cut from four years to three because she admitted the offence early, KBC reports.

items.title: Egyptian author denied US visa wins National Book Award for prison memoir
items.why: Abdelrahman ElGendy won the nonfiction prize in New York on Wednesday for "Huna", a memoir of the more than six years he says he spent as a political prisoner in Egypt. US consular officials denied him a visitor visa, so his editor accepted it.
items.matters: Hannah Lillith Assadi won fiction for "Paradiso 17", about an exiled Palestinian; Salman Rushdie received a lifetime achievement medal.

items.title: US jury convicts pastor over 2021 killing of Haiti's president
items.why: A federal jury in Miami found Haitian-American pastor Christian Emmanuel Sanon guilty on Wednesday on all eight charges over the plot to kill Haiti's President Jovenel Moïse, shot dead at home in July 2021. He faces up to life in prison; sentencing is on 10 February.
items.matters: His lawyer says he will appeal. US prosecutors have charged more than 40 people over the killing.

items.changed: Updated 20 Nov: the court found Myanmar responsible for genocide.
items.title: UN's top court finds Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya
items.why: The International Court of Justice in The Hague ruled 9-6 on Thursday that Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority in a 2017 army crackdown, the first time it has found a state responsible for genocide. It ordered Myanmar to punish those responsible and compensate victims.
items.matters: The ruling is final; Myanmar must report back within two years. About 1.2 million Rohingya refugees live in Bangladesh.

items.title: Van Gogh painting sells for record $190.4m at New York auction
items.why: Vincent van Gogh's "Chestnut Trees in Blossom", painted in 1890, the year he died, sold at Sotheby's in New York on Wednesday for $190.4m including fees. The previous auction record for his work was $117.2m, set in 2022.
items.matters: The sale followed a last-minute settlement with heirs of a German former owner, who say his family sold it under Nazi-era pressure.

items.title: Bancroft says whole Australian team knew of 2018 ball-tampering plot
items.why: Former Australia batter Cameron Bancroft wrote in The West Australian on Wednesday that "the whole team" knew sandpaper was being used on the ball in South Africa in 2018, not only the three players punished. Captain Pat Cummins has called such claims "complete and utter nonsense".
items.matters: Cricket Australia says it will consider his account but will not reopen its investigation.

items.title: US Federal Reserve minutes point to an interest rate rise in December
items.why: Minutes of the US Federal Reserve's October meeting, published on Wednesday, show nearly all policymakers think raising rates again would likely be appropriate to bring inflation back to 2%. The Fed held its key rate at 3.75% to 4% in October after raising it in September.
items.matters: Higher US rates make borrowing dearer around the world; markets see about a 95% chance of a December rise, AP reports.

items.title: US and Venezuela agree to restore military ties during Hegseth visit
items.why: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth announced an agreement on joint training and intelligence sharing during a surprise visit to Venezuela's capital, Caracas, on Wednesday. Interim president Delcy Rodríguez called it a resumption of military ties. She took over after US forces seized Nicolás Maduro in January.
items.matters: Hegseth called Venezuela a "compliant security partner"; few details of the deal have been published.

items.title: Democrats nominate Hakeem Jeffries to be first Black US House speaker
items.why: House Democrats voted 251 to 11 on Wednesday to nominate Hakeem Jeffries of New York as speaker of the US House of Representatives. With Democrats taking control after the midterms, the full House is expected to elect him when it meets on 3 January.

items.title: Fossil teeth show Homo erectus lived in southern China's rainforests
items.why: Eight teeth from two caves near Chongzuo in Guangxi, southern China, belong to Homo erectus and are 184,000 to 324,000 years old, two studies in Nature reported on Wednesday. Chemical traces suggest these early humans lived in rainforest. A ninth tooth is from another, unidentified human species.
items.matters: The species was thought to have vanished from mainland Asia about 400,000 years ago and to have avoided rainforests.

items.title: Astronomers watch a giant star swallow its companion for the first time
items.why: A red giant about 350 times wider than the Sun, in the Andromeda galaxy 2.5 million light-years away, appears to have swallowed a smaller Sun-like star, a team led by Columbia University reported in Nature on Wednesday. NASA's Webb telescope observed the aftermath.
items.matters: Astronomers say both stars may instead have survived in a tighter orbit; further observations should tell.

items.title: Ghana's central bank cuts its main interest rate from 14% to 11%
items.why: The Bank of Ghana lowered its policy rate by three percentage points on Wednesday, to its lowest level in decades. Governor Johnson Pandit Asiama called it "a realignment, not a reduction", because market rates had already fallen below 14%. Inflation was 5.5% in October.
items.matters: Cheaper borrowing could ease costs for Ghanaian households and businesses; average bank lending rates have already fallen to about 16%.

items.changed: Updated 20 Nov: Israel says the operation has ended.
items.title: Israel ends one-day ground operation in central Gaza beyond ceasefire line
items.why: Israel's military said on Thursday it had ended a raid near the Bureij and Nuseirat camps and destroyed part of a Hamas tunnel. Hamas called the incursion a flagrant ceasefire violation. Gaza's Hamas-run health ministry says at least 1,662 people have been killed since the October 2025 truce.
items.matters: Residents ordered out during the raid have returned; Israel says the tunnel threatened its troops.

items.title: EU governments approve trade deal removing most tariffs with Indonesia
items.why: EU member states approved on Wednesday the signing of a trade and investment deal with Indonesia, after talks that began in 2016. Indonesia is to remove 98.5% of its tariffs on EU goods, saving EU exporters more than €600m a year, the Irish Times reports.
items.matters: Both sides want it in force quickly, as Indonesia loses its existing EU tariff preferences on 1 January.

items.title: EU proposes €45bn loan for Ukraine, repayable only from Russian reparations
items.why: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen proposed on Wednesday a €45bn loan to Ukraine for 2027: €20bn for its budget and €25bn for military needs. Ukraine would repay it only once Russia pays for war damage. EU member states must approve it.
items.matters: It would cover about two-thirds of Ukraine's expected €70bn funding gap next year; EU leaders discuss it at next week's summit.

items.title: Antibiotics failing against more hospital infections in Europe, WHO and ECDC warn
items.why: Bloodstream infections with Klebsiella pneumoniae bacteria resistant to last-resort carbapenem antibiotics rose 72% in the EU, Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein between 2019 and 2025, the EU's disease agency ECDC said on Wednesday. The target was a 5% fall. WHO says first-line antibiotics are failing in many countries.
items.matters: Patients whose first antibiotic does not work are more likely to die in hospital, WHO's Marc-Alain Widdowson says.

items.title: Germany cuts electricity tax and plans fuel price cap from January
items.why: Germany's governing coalition agreed on Wednesday, after overnight talks, to cut electricity tax for households and small businesses from 2.05 cents to 0.1 cents per kWh for 2027. It also plans a three-month cap on petrol and diesel prices from 1 January.
items.matters: Energy prices rose after the Iran war disrupted Gulf shipping; the tax cut costs about €5bn a year.

items.title: Senegal's ruling party expels President Faye amid feud with Sonko
items.why: Pastef, which holds 130 of 165 seats in Senegal's parliament, said on Tuesday that President Bassirou Diomaye Faye and 31 others had automatically lost their membership. Faye sacked party leader Ousmane Sonko as prime minister in May; Sonko is now parliament's speaker.
items.matters: The rift has stalled Senegal's budget and an IMF loan programme of about $2.2bn the country is waiting for.

items.title: US says string of tech outages is unrelated and not a cyberattack
items.why: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Wednesday there is "zero evidence" that recent outages are linked or caused by hackers or foreign actors. They include a worldwide Microsoft outage, a nationwide flight ground stop, problems at big US banks and a classified government network going offline.
items.matters: Microsoft and the US aviation regulator blamed technical faults during upgrades and found no sign of malicious activity.

items.title: Italy passes antisemitism law using the IHRA definition
items.why: Italy's lower house gave final approval on Tuesday night, by 147 votes to 93, to a law that adopts the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance definition of antisemitism. It creates no new crimes or penalties. Opponents say it could chill criticism of Israel; the government says such criticism remains protected.
items.matters: Italy's Antisemitism Observatory recorded 963 antisemitic incidents in 2025, almost four times the 2022 figure.

items.title: UK inflation rises to 3.6% as diesel prices hit a record
items.why: Consumer prices in the UK rose 3.6% in the year to October, up from 3.5% in September, the Office for National Statistics said on Wednesday. Motor fuel was 33.2% dearer than a year earlier, with diesel averaging a record 199.5p a litre.
items.matters: Petrol and diesel drove the rise; the ONS says pump prices have eased in November as oil prices fell.

items.title: Arsenic in river from Myanmar mines cuts water to Thai villages
items.why: Thailand's prime minister has ordered officials to find new water sources for more than 20,000 households in Mae Sai, in northern Chiang Rai province. Arsenic in the Sai River has reached up to 28 times the safe limit; researchers link much of it to mining across the border in Myanmar.
items.matters: Officials fear the pollution is spreading into the Mekong, which millions of people in several countries rely on.

items.title: Democrat Mary Peltola wins Alaska Senate seat, the last midterm race decided
items.why: Mary Peltola beat Republican senator Dan Sullivan in Alaska, the AP and NBC News projected late on Tuesday, with about 50% of the vote. It was the last US Senate race of the midterms to be called; Democrats and their independent allies will hold 56 of 100 seats from January.
items.matters: Democrats flipped nine Senate seats this year, their biggest net gain since 1958, and will control the chamber.

items.changed: Updated 20 Nov: shares closed 17% above the offer price on their first day.
items.title: Anthropic shares close 17% above their $83 offer price on debut
items.why: Anthropic, the US company behind the Claude AI models, began trading on Nasdaq on Thursday. Its shares opened at $111.50, 34% above the $83 offer price, then fell back to close at $97.17, up 17%. NBC News says that values the company at about $1.76tn.
items.matters: Al Jazeera calls it the biggest share sale on record; it came as major US share indexes fell about 2%.

items.changed: Updated 20 Nov: the game is out, with reviews and first sales estimates.
items.title: Grand Theft Auto VI launches to near-perfect reviews and record sales estimates
items.why: Rockstar Games' Grand Theft Auto VI went on sale worldwide on Thursday on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, 13 years after GTA V. It scored 99 out of 100 on review site Metacritic. Analytics firm Sensor Tower estimates 19.1 million copies sold by Thursday morning, Reuters reports.
items.matters: Sensor Tower puts first-day revenue at about $1.84bn, more than twice GTA V's in 2013; Take-Two has not given figures.

items.title: Pochettino ends US reign with win before joining Manchester United
items.why: The United States beat Haiti 2-0 in Cincinnati on Tuesday, with goals from Christian Pulisic and 18-year-old Julian Hall, to reach the Concacaf Nations League semi-finals 8-0 on aggregate. It was Mauricio Pochettino's last game as US coach before he takes over at Manchester United.
items.matters: United are 18th in the Premier League; Pochettino's first match is against Liverpool on Sunday.

items.changed: Updated 20 Nov: ECDC now counts 11,504 confirmed cases and 5,630 deaths; vaccine trials start next week.
items.title: WHO says Congo's Ebola outbreak has more than doubled in three months
items.why: WHO head Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said on 17 November that more than 11,000 cases and 5,400 deaths had been reported in eight provinces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The EU's disease agency, ECDC, now counts 11,504 confirmed cases and 5,630 deaths.
items.matters: There is no approved vaccine for this Bundibugyo strain; WHO says trials of two candidates start in Ituri province next week.

items.changed: Updated 20 Nov: the three leaders issued a joint declaration after their talks.
items.title: Trump, Xi and Putin pledge nuclear risk talks at first three-way summit
items.why: Meeting in Shenzhen, China, on Thursday, the three leaders issued a four-point declaration promising dialogue on reducing nuclear risks, more refined oil supplies, UN reform and opposition to "abuse" by the International Criminal Court. It did not mention the wars in Ukraine or Iran.
items.matters: The declaration set no limits on nuclear arsenals; Trump has invited Putin to next month's G20 summit in Miami, Al Jazeera reports.

items.changed: Updated 20 Nov: parliament accepted the resignation.
items.title: Mongolia's parliament accepts president's resignation over corruption allegations
items.why: Mongolia's parliament voted on Thursday, by 96 of 104 members present, to accept President Khurelsukh Ukhnaa's resignation with immediate effect. A former mayor of the capital, Ulaanbaatar, accused him of receiving $25m linked to a 2019 railway contract; he denies wrongdoing.
items.matters: Parliament speaker Byambatsogt Sandag acts as president; an election must be called within four months.

items.changed: Updated 20 Nov: the bridge was hit again on Thursday, halting trains.
items.title: Ukraine strikes Crimea bridge for a third time in a week
items.why: Russia suspended trains on the Kerch Bridge to annexed Crimea after another overnight drone attack on Thursday, its transport ministry says; Crimea's Russian-installed governor said service would resume that afternoon. A road span collapsed after Ukrainian strikes on Tuesday, and road traffic remains halted.
items.matters: Putin has vowed to retaliate; Russia's deputy prime minister says some sections may reopen within one or two months.

items.changed: Updated 19 Nov: Bahrain says it intercepted Iranian attacks for the third time in a week.
items.title: Iran targets US base in Kuwait after American strike on Qeshm Island
items.why: Iran's army says its drones targeted US air-defence systems at Kuwait's Ali Al Salem air base on Wednesday, after US jets hit a missile site on Iran's Qeshm Island on Tuesday. Kuwait and Bahrain say they intercepted the attacks. The US military says no US personnel were hurt.
items.matters: Qatar, a mediator, calls it a dangerous escalation; the Trump–Xi–Putin declaration did not mention the Iran war.
